original_question: Find a general property of a lifting family in the interval version of Thurston’s algorithm that guarantees convergence for all preperiodic or periodic kneading sequences.
target_in_paper: §3, Thurston's algorithm for real functions, Question 3 (page 9): Give a general property for the lifting family which will guarantee convergence of Thurston's algorithm for preperiodic or periodic kneading sequences.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact official target very closely: it asks for a general property of the lifting family, in the interval/real-function version of Thurston's algorithm, with the scope restricted to periodic or preperiodic kneading sequences. That is precisely the content of Question 3 in §3.
missing_details: The ambient dynamical space is not stated: one works in P = P(n, mu), the space of piecewise monotone maps f of the interval I = [0,1] having n laps and sending the boundary {0,1} into itself according to a prescribed boundary map mu.
The phrase "lifting family" is left implicit. In context it means a family inside P used in place of the degree-n polynomial subfamily in the lifting step of the algorithm.

The iterative procedure itself is not specified. Starting from f_0 in P, one chooses a lift p_k with the same critical values as f_k, encountered in the same order, then takes the homeomorphism h_k:[0,1]->[0,1] carrying the critical points of f_k to those of p_k and satisfying p_k o h_k = f_k, and sets f_{k+1} = h_k o f_k o h_k^{-1}.
The quantifier should be attached to the initial map f_0 (or to the kneading sequence realized by f_0), not just to kneading sequences in the abstract.

The intended sense of "convergence" is implicit. In the immediately preceding discussion, convergence means convergence of the Thurston iteration in the polynomial case, where the lift maps p_k converge to a limit p_infinity with the same kneading sequence as f_0; your draft does not state this contextual benchmark.

The paper treats the broader case of arbitrary kneading sequences separately as Question 4, so the refined question should explicitly remain restricted to the periodic/preperiodic case and not drift into the arbitrary case.

There is no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree-of-polynomial algebraic restriction, or nilpotency condition here; the essential omitted data are dynamical and algorithmic, namely the space P(n, mu), the interval I = [0,1], the lift-selection rule, and the iteration scheme.
refined_question: In the setting of §3, let P = P(n, mu) be the space of piecewise monotone maps f:I=[0,1]->I with n laps and prescribed boundary action mu on {0,1}. Starting from f_0 in P, modify Thurston's interval algorithm by replacing the polynomial lift with a lift chosen from a fixed family F subset P: at each stage choose p_k in F having the same critical values as f_k, encountered in the same order, let h_k:[0,1]->[0,1] be the homeomorphism carrying the critical points of f_k to those of p_k and satisfying p_k o h_k = f_k, and define f_{k+1} = h_k o f_k o h_k^{-1}. What general structural property of the lifting family F guarantees convergence of this modified Thurston algorithm whenever the initial map f_0 has a periodic or preperiodic kneading sequence?
justification: The draft points to the exact official item in this paper: §3 is titled "Thurston's algorithm for real functions," and Question 3 on page 9 asks verbatim for a general property of the lifting family guaranteeing convergence for preperiodic or periodic kneading sequences. The nearby setup on pages 8-9 defines the ambient space P = P(n, mu), the interval I = [0,1], the polynomial lifting step via matching critical values in the same order, the conjugacies h_k, and the induced iteration f_{k+1} = h_k o f_k o h_k^{-1}. The paragraph immediately before Questions 2-4 explains the intended convergence benchmark in the polynomial case, and Question 2 gives the motivating nonpolynomial family x -> k - k|2x-1|^alpha. Question 4 then shows that extending from periodic/preperiodic kneading data to arbitrary kneading sequences is a distinct broader problem. Since this paper is a problem list rather than a theorem paper with Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3, the correct paper-faithful target is precisely Question 3 of §3.
